claims.statement: CTIS supplies searchable public trial facts and downloadable search or trial records, which is enough for a public-data prototype but not evidence of site-level startup, recruitment-delivery, query-burden, or closeout performance.

The EU clinical-trial transparency regime expressly protects personal data and commercially confidential information, so non-public operational outcomes require separate authority, contractual permissions, minimisation, and disclosure controls.

Published research supports startup speed, recruitment, patient access, and data quality as relevant site-selection or performance dimensions, but it does not validate one portable score or prove that Polish sites and CROs will share the required data.

Citeline, IQVIA, and Medidata already market sophisticated feasibility, site-selection, site-performance, workflow, and proprietary-data products, making generic site discovery or ranking an unattractive wedge.

It remains an unvalidated hypothesis that a site-owned, permissioned operational evidence passport with transparent definitions and appeals will induce contributions and create a buyer willingness to pay distinct from incumbent feasibility suites.

contrary_evidence: Major vendors already advertise proprietary site-level performance, enrollment, quality, workflow, and API capabilities.
CTIS public records do not contain the private operational outcomes that would make a reliability history valuable.
The published performance literature supports benchmarking but does not establish a fair cross-sponsor attribution method or a commercial exchange.
Public pricing was not found for the enterprise incumbents, so the proposed price and acquisition assumptions cannot be benchmarked reliably.

economics.acquisition_route: Build a CTIS-derived Polish site map and a private, site-controlled evidence-packet workflow; validate with one therapeutic area and seek a paid, bounded feasibility pilot before building shared scoring or integrations.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Planning hypothesis, not forecast: reaching about 800 paying site-tool accounts at 8000 PLN annual revenue plus 50 buyer accounts at 100000 PLN annual revenue would produce roughly 11.4M PLN ARR. At 22% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 60% founder ownership, equity would be about 6.0M PLN, plausibly in year 7-10 only if contribution and renewal loops are proven. Retained cash is not added again.
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly for the public-data prototype and one bounded pilot; security, clinical-operations methodology, and privacy review must be contracted rather than improvised.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Planning range of 55-70% during manually verified pilots and 70-80% only after standardised ingestion, sampling, and appeals; no evidence yet supports either range.
economics.payback: Unknown until a paid pilot reveals sales-cycle length, security-review cost, and renewal value; cap pre-contract build and selling spend at the stated bootstrap budget.
economics.pricing: Test a 10000-25000 PLN scoped feasibility packet, then hypotheses of 300-800 PLN per site per month for workflow tools and 40000-100000 PLN per buyer per year for permissioned intelligence; never sell a higher rank.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Potential repeat events are new-study feasibility, annual preferred-site review, and ongoing evidence updates, but neither renewal nor contribution frequency is validated.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned longitudinal operational evidence owned or attested by sites, with definitions, sample thresholds, provenance, and an appeal trail
fingerprint.customer: Independent Polish clinical-trial sites seeking portable evidence and CRO or sponsor feasibility teams that lack trustworthy local operational history
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: CTIS-derived public profiles, self-serve evidence packets, therapeutic-area site associations, and later buyer workflow exports
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Free public-data site map, paid site evidence workflow, and contributor-gated buyer feasibility packets without public punitive scoring
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Site pays for private workflow tools; CRO or sponsor pays for a bounded feasibility packet or annual permissioned access, never for influence over a credential
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A site prepares for outreach or a buyer begins country and site feasibility for a new study

founder_fit: Data provenance, uncertainty, normalization, and auditability fit the founder's data-science skills.
Neuroscience training and medical adjacency help with terminology while contracted clinical-operations expertise remains necessary.
A CTIS prototype can be built part-time without patient data or immediate enterprise integration.
Self-serve evidence packets reduce reliance on public-facing content, although initial enterprise discovery still requires bounded interviews and sales.
risks: Unfair attribution or a thin-sample score could damage a site's reputation; private evidence packets, minimum samples, uncertainty bands, and appeals are essential.
Sponsors, CROs, and sites may lack the right or incentive to contribute comparable operational data.
Enterprise incumbents can bundle similar features with broader proprietary datasets and existing procurement relationships.
Information-security and vendor-assessment cycles may be incompatible with a lightly resourced part-time launch.

structure.commercial_archetype: site-owned evidence passport and contributor-gated feasibility exchange
structure.control_point: Permissioned, portable operational evidence with provenance, normalisation, and appeal rights
structure.critical_dependency: Enough sites and buyers must lawfully contribute comparable outcomes and treat the resulting evidence as decision-useful

thesis: Create a Polish clinical-trial site evidence passport: CTIS supplies a public factual profile, while each site privately assembles permissioned, study-normalised evidence on startup, recruitment delivery, data queries, and closeout. Sites choose what to share in a feasibility packet; buyer access is gated and no public or pay-to-rank score is launched until attribution, sample size, and appeals are validated.
title: TrialSite Evidence Passport for Poland
uncertainties: Whether sites possess contractual rights to reuse sponsor or CRO operational metrics in a portable packet.
Whether buyers will accept site-attested data and what independent verification is proportionate.
The minimum cohort needed for useful normalization by therapeutic area and study complexity.
Enterprise sales cycle, security requirements, public-data update burden, and public-versus-private data licensing boundaries.
Willingness to pay, contribution rate, renewal, acquisition cost, and gross margin.
